Sentiment measures opinion, not entities.
Summarisation shortens text rather than tagging entities.

PII detection finds personal data, not opinions.

Entity linking disambiguates entities.
Abstractive summaries rephrase content in new wording.
Opinion mining is aspect-level sentiment.

Key phrases list concepts without disambiguation.

Sentiment measures opinion.

Temperature affects text generation randomness, not voice output.
Batch transcription converts audio to text.

Switch to speech synthesis with a custom voice

questions.scenario: A tested agent must now be called by a production web app through an endpoint that does not change when the agent is updated.
questions.stem: What should the team do?
options: Share the playground URL with developers
Export the agent as a PDF
Publish the agent to get a stable endpoint with automatic version snapshots
Recreate the agent as a hosted agent
questions.explanation: Publishing gives the agent a stable endpoint, and versions are snapshotted automatically. Applications and channels such as Teams can then call it.
rationales: The playground is for testing, not production integration.
A PDF cannot be called by an application.
Correct. Publishing gives a stable endpoint.
Changing agent type is unnecessary.

questions.scenario: A security architect is reviewing a customer-facing agent that reads emails and web pages through its tools.
questions.stem: Which two measures are supported by Foundry Agent Service to reduce risk? (Select two.)
options: Keep content filters on to mitigate prompt injection, including cross-prompt injection (XPIA)
Give the agent's dedicated Microsoft Entra identity least-privilege RBAC roles
Put an admin API key in the agent instructions so tools always succeed
Turn off content filters to reduce latency
questions.explanation: Each agent has its own Entra identity controlled with RBAC, so it should get least privilege. Content filters help mitigate prompt injection, including cross-prompt injection hidden in documents or tool results.
rationales: Correct. Filters mitigate direct and cross-prompt injection.
Correct. Least privilege limits the damage if the agent is compromised.
Secrets in instructions can be leaked through prompt injection.
Turning off filters removes injection protection.

questions.scenario: A team notices unexpected charges after a week of heavy testing in the agents playground, even though it ran few production calls.
questions.stem: What is a likely contributing cause?
options: Traces are stored in a Provisioned deployment
Evaluations are on by default in the agents playground and are billed
File search is billed per character of the instructions
The playground always uses a Batch deployment
questions.explanation: In the agents playground, evaluations run by default and are billed. That can add cost during heavy testing.
rationales: Traces are not stored in deployments.
Correct. Default evaluations add cost.
File search searches uploaded files; it is not described as billed by the length of the instructions.
The playground does not force Batch deployments.

questions.scenario: A developer is building a lightweight Python client that must hold a multi-turn conversation with a published Foundry agent.
questions.stem: Which approach matches the current platform?
options: AIProjectClient with the project endpoint, get_openai_client(), and Responses API calls that target the agent within a conversation
A Content Understanding analyzer with a Generate field
Assistants API threads and runs with polling
questions.explanation: Foundry agents are built on the Responses API, and clients use the project client to get an OpenAI client. Conversations keep multi-turn state, replacing the older Assistants threads.
rationales: Correct. This is the current pattern for agent clients.
Question answering is a legacy Language feature, not an agent client.
Analyzers extract content; they do not chat with agents.
This is the replaced Assistants API model.

sources.title: Foundry Agent Service overview — Microsoft Foundry

questions.scenario: A developer wants to quickly try an agent definition (model, instructions, one tool) from code without creating a persisted agent in the portal.
questions.stem: Which option fits?
options: An ephemeral agent: call the Responses API directly with the definition in code
questions.explanation: Ephemeral agents are defined in your code and called directly through the Responses API, without a persisted agent. Hosted agents package your own code as a container or .zip.
rationales: A deployment type does not define an agent.
Correct. The definition lives in code.
This is heavier than needed and still creates a deployed agent.
Analyzers are for extraction.

questions.scenario: A developer is building an agent in the Foundry portal.
questions.stem: Which two of the following are built-in agent tools? (Select two.)
questions.explanation: Foundry Agent Service lists web search, file search, code interpreter and memory as built-in tools. Batch transcription is an Azure Speech feature and prebuilt-invoice is a Content Understanding analyzer.
rationales: Correct. A built-in tool for running code.

questions.scenario: A developer has a working configuration in the model playground (deployment, system instructions, file search) and wants to turn it into an agent with as little rework as possible.
questions.stem: What should they do?
options: Rebuild it as a hosted agent container
Use Save as agent from the playground
questions.explanation: The model playground includes a Save as agent option that turns the current configuration into an agent. The other options need more work or are unrelated.
rationales: A hosted container is unnecessary rework.
Correct. Save as agent reuses the configuration.
Batch jobs are for bulk asynchronous inference.
Speech Studio is for speech features.

questions.scenario: A contact center must remove names, phone numbers and account numbers from chat transcripts before storing them.
questions.stem: Which Azure Language feature should it use?
questions.explanation: PII detection is a core Azure Language feature that finds and redacts personal information. Key phrase extraction and entity linking do not redact.
rationales: This only identifies the language.
This links entities to Wikipedia.
Correct. It detects and redacts personal data.
This returns main concepts, not redactions.

questions.scenario: An app receives customer emails in many languages and must route each one to the right regional team.
questions.stem: Which capability identifies the language of each email?
questions.explanation: Language detection is a core Azure Language feature that identifies the language of a text. The other options are speech or image features.
rationales: This edits images.
This turns text into audio.
Correct.
This adapts speech recognition.

questions.scenario: A legal team wants a new app that lists the people, organizations, locations and dates mentioned in contracts.
questions.stem: Which Azure Language feature is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Named entity recognition identifies and categorizes entities such as people, organizations, locations and dates, and it is a core feature for new development. Entity linking maps entities to Wikipedia entries.
rationales: Entity linking maps entities to Wikipedia, which is not what the team needs.
Correct. NER categorizes entities.
Sentiment measures opinion.
Summarization shortens text.

questions.scenario: A hospital wants to extract conditions, medications and dosages from unstructured clinical notes.
questions.stem: Which feature is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Text Analytics for health is a core Azure Language feature that extracts medical entities from clinical text. General key phrases do not label medical concepts.
rationales: Translation changes the language, not the structure.
Key phrases are generic and not medically labelled.
Correct.
Prompt Shields detects prompt attacks.

questions.scenario: An architect reviews a proposal for a new conversational app.
questions.stem: Which two proposed services should be rejected because they are retired? (Select two.)
questions.explanation: LUIS and QnA Maker are retired, along with Personalizer, Anomaly Detector, Content Moderator and Metrics Advisor. Translator and Speech are current Foundry Tools.
rationales: Translator is a current Foundry Tool.
Speech is a current Foundry Tool.
Correct. Retired.
Correct. Retired.

questions.scenario: A company must translate 5,000 Word and PDF files into French while keeping their formatting.
questions.stem: Which approach is appropriate?
options: Translator text translation, one paragraph at a time
Translator asynchronous batch document translation, using Azure Blob Storage
questions.explanation: Translator document translation translates whole files while keeping their structure, and the asynchronous batch mode uses Azure Blob Storage. Text translation is for strings and would lose document formatting.
rationales: Detection does not translate.
This works on text strings and loses file formatting.
Speech translation is for audio.
Correct. Batch document translation uses Blob Storage.

questions.scenario: Managers want summaries of long support chats written as fresh, concise sentences rather than copied lines.
questions.stem: Which summarization style matches?
questions.explanation: Abstractive summarization writes new sentences, while extractive summarization selects existing sentences from the source. Key phrases are only a list of concepts.
rationales: Extractive copies existing sentences.
This links entities to Wikipedia.
Key phrases are not a summary.
Correct. It writes new sentences.

questions.scenario: You are building a new text analytics app in 2026 and want to start from Azure Language features recommended for new development.
questions.stem: Which two are core (not legacy) Azure Language features? (Select two.)
questions.explanation: Azure Language lists PII detection, language detection, NER and Text Analytics for health as core features. Key phrase extraction and sentiment analysis are legacy features that remain supported for existing solutions.
rationales: Legacy feature.
Correct. A core feature.
Correct. A core feature.
Legacy feature.

questions.scenario: A conference wants live captions displayed on screen as speakers talk.
questions.stem: Which speech-to-text option fits?
questions.explanation: Real-time transcription converts live audio into text as it is spoken. Batch transcription processes stored audio asynchronously.
rationales: This creates synthetic voices.
Batch is asynchronous, for stored files.
Correct.
This is the opposite direction.

questions.scenario: An insurer has 80,000 archived call recordings in storage and wants transcripts by the end of the week. Latency per file is not important.
questions.stem: Which option should it use?
questions.explanation: Batch transcription processes large volumes of stored audio asynchronously through REST. Real-time transcription is meant for live streams.
rationales: Correct.
This scores pronunciation.
This is for live audio, not large archives.
This is for real-time voice conversations.

questions.scenario: A notes app lets a user upload one recorded voice memo and should show the transcript within seconds.
questions.stem: Which option is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Fast transcription gives quick, synchronous transcription of a pre-recorded file. Batch is asynchronous and meant for large volumes.
rationales: Translation is not requested.
Custom voice is for synthesis.
Batch suits large asynchronous jobs, not a single file needed in seconds.
Correct.

questions.scenario: A voice app mispronounces a brand name and talks too fast for elderly users.
questions.stem: What should the developer use?
options: A higher temperature on the chat model
SSML to adjust pronunciation and speaking rate
questions.explanation: SSML tunes synthesized speech, including pronunciation, speaking rate, pitch and volume. The other options do not affect speech output.
rationales: Temperature changes text generation, not voice output.
This identifies a language.
This is speech to text.
Correct.

questions.scenario: A factory voice-command app misrecognizes machine part names because of heavy background noise and specialized vocabulary.
questions.stem: What is the best improvement?
options: Use SSML on the input audio
Train a custom speech model with acoustic and language data
questions.explanation: Custom speech models are trained with acoustic, language or pronunciation data to improve accuracy in noisy settings and with domain jargon. Batch mode and SSML do not improve recognition.
rationales: Batch changes the processing mode, not accuracy.
SSML applies to speech synthesis, not recognition.
Correct.
This is a text generation setting.

questions.scenario: A product team wants customers to have natural, low-latency, two-way spoken conversations with an agent.
questions.stem: Which Azure Speech capability is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Voice Live supports real-time voice conversations between people and agents, and voice-based prompt agents use it. The other options are batch or scoring features.
rationales: This is asynchronous and offline.
Correct.
This scores pronunciation.
This is a Translator feature for files.

questions.scenario: A team builds a voice assistant. It wants as few components as possible, and the model should interpret the user's spoken question directly rather than a transcript.
questions.stem: Which design best meets these goals?
options: Speech to text, then a text model, then text to speech, each as separate services
Send the recorded audio to a deployed multimodal model that accepts audio input
Use a Content Understanding receipt analyzer
questions.explanation: A deployed multimodal model that accepts audio can respond to spoken prompts directly, so fewer services are needed. A speech pipeline gives finer control over each stage but has more moving parts.
rationales: This is valid but adds components and works from a transcript.
Translation does not answer questions.
Correct. The model receives the audio itself.
This extracts receipt data.

questions.stem: Which Azure Speech capability fits?

questions.scenario: An insurance app lets customers upload a photo of a damaged car. The app must describe the damage in plain language for a claims agent.
questions.stem: What is the recommended approach for a new build?

questions.explanation: Including the image in the prompt to a multimodal model lets the model interpret the photo and describe it. Image Analysis 4.0 is deprecated and DALL-E 3 is retired.

This is deprecated and not recommended for new solutions.

questions.stem: Which model family should it plan to use?
questions.explanation: DALL-E 3 is retired, and image generation in Foundry uses the gpt-image series through the playground, the Images API or the Responses API.

questions.scenario: A designer has a product photo and wants to replace only the background with a beach scene, keeping the product unchanged.
questions.stem: Which technique fits?
options: Generate a new image from text only
Image editing (inpainting) with a mask over the background and a prompt describing the beach
questions.explanation: Inpainting changes only the masked region of an existing image based on a prompt. Generating from text alone would not keep the original product.
rationales: OCR extracts text.
This creates a completely new image.
Correct. The mask limits changes to the background.
Face detection finds faces.

options: Images can be generated through the Images API or the Responses API
DALL-E 3 is the recommended model for new solutions
Image generation requires an Azure Speech resource
The Foundry portal provides an images playground for trying image models
questions.explanation: Foundry supports image generation through the Images API, the Responses API and the images playground. DALL-E 3 is retired, and Speech is unrelated.
rationales: Correct.
DALL-E 3 is retired.

questions.scenario: A team wants to build new scene-description features and is considering Image Analysis 4.0 because an older tutorial used it.
questions.stem: What should you advise?
options: Use QnA Maker for image questions
Image Analysis 4.0 is deprecated; use a multimodal model (or Content Understanding for structured extraction)
Use Personalizer to rank image captions
Image Analysis 4.0 is the newest vision API
questions.explanation: Image Analysis 4.0 is deprecated with a published retirement date, and Image Analysis and OCR are labelled legacy. New vision features should use multimodal models or Content Understanding.
rationales: QnA Maker is retired and text-only.
Correct.
Personalizer is retired.
It is deprecated, not new.

questions.scenario: A public image app lets users upload photos that are then described by a multimodal model.
questions.stem: Which capability helps block images containing violent or sexual content?
options: Azure AI Content Safety harm categories, applied through Foundry guardrails
questions.explanation: Content Safety, which powers Foundry guardrails, checks text and images across the hate, sexual, violence and self-harm categories, each with severity levels.
rationales: Correct.
This extracts document layout.
This is for speech recognition.
Translator does not moderate images.

questions.stem: Which Content Safety capability is designed to detect this?

questions.scenario: An accounts payable team wants to pull vendor, invoice number, totals and line items from PDF invoices with minimal setup.
questions.stem: Which Content Understanding analyzer should it start with?
questions.explanation: prebuilt-invoice is a domain analyzer built for invoice fields. prebuilt-read only extracts text, without invoice-specific fields.
rationales: This extracts text only, with no invoice fields.
This analyzes call recordings.
Correct.
This prepares video for search.

questions.scenario: A developer creates a custom analyzer for a company-specific inspection form and tries to set prebuilt-invoice as its parent. The configuration is rejected.
questions.stem: Which parent should they use?
questions.explanation: Only the base analyzers (prebuilt-document, prebuilt-image, prebuilt-audio and prebuilt-video) can be parents of custom analyzers. A form is a document.
rationales: Composed analyzers cannot be parents.
Domain analyzers cannot be parents.
RAG analyzers cannot be parents.
Correct. Base analyzer for documents.

questions.scenario: A digitization project only needs the text and layout of scanned pages and wants to avoid the cost of generative models.
questions.stem: Which analyzer fits?
options: A custom analyzer with Generate fields
questions.explanation: The content extraction analyzers (prebuilt-read and prebuilt-layout) extract text and layout without needing an LLM. The other options rely on generative features.
rationales: This prepares content for search and uses generative features.
Contract field extraction uses generative features.
Correct. No LLM is needed.
Generate fields need an LLM.

questions.scenario: A media company wants each video in its library to include a short free-form description of every scene.
questions.stem: Which field generation method should the schema use?
questions.explanation: Generate fields produce free-form output such as summaries or scene descriptions. Extract only applies to documents, and Classify chooses from fixed categories.
rationales: Classify picks from predefined categories.
Correct.
Translate is not a field method.
Extract is for documents only.

questions.scenario: A call analytics app must label each recorded call as "resolved", "escalated" or "abandoned".
questions.stem: Which field generation method is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Classify fields choose from predefined categories. Generate produces free-form text, and Extract applies only to documents.
rationales: Correct.
Extract is document-only and pulls existing values.
Segmentation splits content; it is not a field method.
Free-form output could fall outside the fixed labels.

questions.scenario: An extraction app must send any field it is unsure about to a human reviewer and show where in the document the value came from.
questions.stem: What should the developer enable?
options: A higher temperature on the analyzer model
questions.explanation: estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence returns confidence scores from 0 to 1 and grounding information. Low-confidence values can then be routed to review along with where they came from.
rationales: Correct.
Translation does not help here.
Segmentation alone does not give confidence or grounding.
Temperature does not produce confidence scores.

questions.scenario: A developer creates a custom analyzer with Generate fields, but analysis fails because no generative model is available.
questions.stem: What is missing?
options: The analyzer needs your own Foundry model deployments (an LLM plus embeddings)
questions.explanation: For generative features, Content Understanding uses Foundry model deployments that you supply: an LLM and an embeddings model. It does not include a hidden model of its own.
rationales: Correct.
Hub projects are classic and are not required.
Translator is unrelated.
Speech is unrelated.

questions.scenario: A team is evaluating Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools for a new pipeline.
questions.stem: Which three input types can it analyze? (Select three.)
options: Live two-way voice conversations with an agent
questions.explanation: Content Understanding analyzes documents, images, audio and video, and outputs Markdown or structured JSON. Real-time voice conversations are handled by Azure Speech Voice Live.
rationales: Correct.
This is a Voice Live scenario, not an extraction modality.
Correct.
Correct.

questions.scenario: A downstream system expects extracted invoice data as fields that match a defined schema.
questions.stem: Which Content Understanding output fits?
options: Structured JSON that matches the field schema
questions.explanation: Content Understanding outputs Markdown or structured JSON that matches your schema. The other formats belong to other services.
rationales: Correct.
Glossaries are for translation.
Audio is not extraction output.
SSML is for speech synthesis.

questions.scenario: A team is moving a Content Understanding app from proof of concept to production.
questions.stem: Which API version strategy is recommended?
options: Always use the newest preview in production
Avoid versioning by calling the portal URL
Target the GA API version for production, and keep preview versions for trying new features
Use whichever version the first tutorial showed
questions.explanation: The GA API version is intended for production workloads, and preview versions add experimental capabilities. Production code should pin to GA.
rationales: Preview versions are not meant for production.
The portal is not an API.
Correct.
Tutorials can be outdated.

questions.scenario: A company wants to make its training video library searchable in a RAG chatbot.
questions.stem: Which analyzer is designed to prepare video content for search?
questions.explanation: The RAG analyzers (prebuilt-documentSearch, imageSearch, audioSearch and videoSearch) prepare content for search and retrieval. The others are document-focused.
rationales: This is for receipts.
This is for identity documents.
This extracts text from documents.
Correct.

questions.scenario: A mailroom app receives a mix of invoices, receipts and contracts in one inbox and must extract the right fields from each.
questions.stem: What is the best design?
options: Use one Generate field to describe each document
Translate every file first, then use language detection
Classify each file with the Analyze API, then route it to the matching domain analyzer
questions.explanation: Classification is part of the unified Analyze API and supports classify-then-route workflows to domain analyzers such as invoice, receipt and contract. One analyzer for all types would miss fields.
rationales: Free-form descriptions do not give structured fields.
Translation does not identify document types or extract fields.
Receipts and contracts would be misparsed.
Correct.

questions.scenario: A support center wants summaries and outcome labels from recorded customer calls using a prebuilt analyzer.
questions.stem: Which analyzer should it evaluate first?
questions.explanation: prebuilt-callCenter is a domain analyzer for call recordings. The other options target documents or images.
rationales: Correct.
This extracts document layout.
This is for invoices.
This prepares images for search.
